item.title: Hermes Desktop Full Guide: Every Setting Explained (5 You Must Change Today)
item.description:
Hermes Desktop told me something about my own PC that I didn’t know. My everyday model, Qwen 3.8 27B, doesn’t fully fit on my RTX 4070’s 12 GB of VRAM. Part of it spills into system RAM, which makes it slower. I found that on a Settings page I had never opened, so I went through all of them.

This post covers every page in Hermes Desktop (v0.23.3 on Windows): what each one does, what I set it to, and what you can skip on a free, local setup. At the end are the 5 settings I’d change today.

This is Part 3 of the series. Part 1 is the Hermes + Ollama + Qwen 3.8 setup on Windows, and Part 2 is controlling Hermes from your phone with Telegram.

🎥 Watch the Video

👉 Watch on YouTube: Hermes Desktop Full Guide

🎮 Does Your Model Even Fit on Your GPU?

Qwen 3.8 27B is roughly a 17 GB download. My graphics card has 12 GB, so Ollama keeps part of the model in normal RAM. It still works, just slower. Hermes Desktop shows this on its Local Models page, which we’ll get to in the Providers section.

🧭 Two Places to Know

Hermes keeps things in two places:

  • The main sidebar (left) is about what Hermes can do: Capabilities, Messaging, Artifacts and Scheduled jobs.
  • Settings (Ctrl + ,) is about how Hermes behaves. It has 22 pages, from Model down to About.

🧩 The Main Sidebar

Capabilities

There are four tabs:

  • Skills: a catalog of skills you can switch on, grouped by topic.
  • Plugins and Connectors: add features and link outside apps.
  • Tools: an on/off switch for every tool Hermes can use, including files, browser automation, code execution, memory, the terminal, cron jobs and web search.

If Hermes ever behaves strangely, check here first to see which skills and tools are on.

Messaging

Hermes can connect to Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Slack, Signal, email, SMS and more. For Telegram there’s now a Quick setup → Create with QR button. You scan, confirm in Telegram, and Hermes creates the bot and detects your user ID. In Part 2 I did this the manual way.

Whichever way you do it, keep Allowed user IDs limited to your own ID and never leave it empty.

Scheduled jobs

This is where Hermes works without you typing anything. It comes with templates such as Morning briefing, Important mail monitor, Weekly review, Topic news digest, and Bills and renewals. Pick one and set a time.

🤖 Model

Model → Main model is the default model for new chats:

  • Provider: custom (our Ollama endpoint)
  • Model: qwen3.8:27b
  • Reasoning: Medium
  • Main model context window (override): 0, which means Hermes uses the context it detects from the model

Click Apply. Until you do, nothing changes.

Hermes needs at least 64K of context, so check the real value with ollama ps (below) instead of guessing.

The Model section has four more pages:

Page What it does For a free local setup
Fallback models Backup model if the main one fails Optional
Auxiliary models Small jobs: chat titles, vision, compression Leave on “use main model”
Subagents Helper agents for big jobs Keep the count low on 12 GB
Mixture of Agents Several cloud models answer together Skip, it isn’t free

🦙 Providers: Connect Ollama

Go to Providers → Custom Endpoints and add Ollama:

Field Value
Endpoint URL http://localhost:11434/v1
API mode Auto-detect
Default model qwen3.8:27b
API key Leave blank

Click Test, then Save. If the test fails, Ollama usually isn’t running, so start it and test again.

Local Models: the page that checks your PC

Providers → Local Models detected my RTX 4070 (12 GB) and 31.2 GB of RAM. It then labels each model: some say “Uses system RAM”, and the biggest say “Too big for this machine”.

To confirm it yourself, run this in PowerShell while the model is loaded:

1

ollama ps
  • PROCESSOR shows whether the model runs fully on the GPU or is split between CPU and GPU.
  • CONTEXT should be 64K or more for Hermes.

If your model is split, you can accept the slower speed or switch to a smaller Qwen.

🧠 Memory and Context

These two pages are easy to mix up:

  • Persistent memory is what Hermes remembers about you across chats, such as facts and a short user profile.
  • Context & compression is what fits inside one chat. When a conversation gets long, Hermes summarizes the older messages.

Tip for local models: if your model is slow, raise Compression model timeout (default 120 seconds).

🛡️ Safety

Approval mode decides what Hermes does before running commands:

  • Manual: asks every time.
  • Smart: asks only for risky commands. This is what I use.
  • Off: never asks. Avoid it, because an agent that runs any command without asking can also delete the wrong folder without asking.

Under Checkpoints, turn on File checkpoints. Hermes then saves a snapshot before it edits your files, so you can roll back. It’s off by default.

🗂️ Workspace, Sessions and Browser

  • Workspace: your default project folder, and which folders Hermes scans for Git projects.
  • Sessions: auto-archive old chats to keep the sidebar clean.
  • Browser: “Use my real browser profile” lets Hermes use your saved logins. It’s off by default, and I’d leave it off unless you really need it.

⚡ Advanced

  • Desktop & startup → Keep computer awake: Off, While working or Always. Telegram and scheduled jobs only work while the PC is awake, so I use While working. This page also has Quick Entry, a small chat box you can open from anywhere, and Run onboarding again.
  • Terminal backend: where commands run. Local (your PC) is the default. Docker runs them in a sandbox, and Modal and Daytona are cloud sandboxes. The command timeout defaults to 180 seconds.
  • Agent limits, Tool access, Output limits: finer controls. The defaults are fine to start with.

🌐 Gateways and Web Access

  • Gateways decides where Hermes runs. Local gateway (this PC, works offline) is the default. The other options are Hermes Cloud, a remote gateway on another machine, or your own server over SSH.
  • Web access lets you open Hermes from your phone’s browser on the same Wi-Fi. The connection isn’t encrypted on your network, so use it only at home.

🎨 The Quick Ones

  • Chat: personality, time zone, and Reasoning Blocks, which shows or hides the model’s thinking.
  • Appearance: language, theme, fonts, layout.
  • Voice: read replies aloud, speech to text, text to speech.
  • Notifications: desktop alerts, for example when Hermes needs your approval.
  • Keyboard Shortcuts: every binding can be changed. Remember Ctrl + , (Settings) and Ctrl + K (search).
  • Backup & Transfer: saves your whole agent (profiles, settings, memory, skills, schedules and chats) to one file. Do this once you’ve finished setting up.
  • About: your version, update checks and uninstall.

🗑️ What You Can Skip on a Free Setup

  • Billing: $0 on the Free plan, which is fine for a local setup.
  • Mixture of Agents and Hermes Cloud: these need cloud models or an account.
  • Tools & Keys: only needed for paid add-on tools such as search APIs.
  • Fallback models: an optional backup.
  • Passwords & Logins: leave it alone, and never open it on camera.

🏆 My 5 Must-Change Settings

  1. Providers: add Ollama as a Custom Endpoint, then click Test.
  2. Model: set Qwen 3.8 as the main model, then click Apply.
  3. Local Models + ollama ps: check that your model actually fits on your GPU.
  4. Safety: set Approval mode to Smart and turn on File checkpoints.
  5. Advanced: set Keep computer awake to While working.

❓ FAQ

Where is the context window setting in Hermes Desktop?

In Settings → Model → Main model, under “Main model context window (override)”. 0 means Hermes uses the context it detects from the model. Check the real value with ollama ps, since Hermes needs at least 64K.

How do I connect Hermes Desktop to Ollama?

Go to Settings → Providers → Custom Endpoints, use http://localhost:11434/v1 as the endpoint URL, leave API mode on Auto-detect and the API key blank, then click Test and Save.

Does Qwen 3.8 27B fit on a 12 GB GPU?

Not fully. It’s roughly 17 GB, so on a 12 GB card like the RTX 4070 part of it runs from system RAM, and Hermes Desktop’s Local Models page labels it “Uses system RAM”. Run ollama ps and check the PROCESSOR column to see the split.

Which approval mode should I use in Hermes?

Smart, which asks only for risky commands. Manual asks every time, and Off never asks, which isn’t safe for an agent that can run commands on your PC.

Do I need to pay for anything in Hermes Desktop?

No. With Ollama and a local model, the Billing page shows $0 on the Free plan. Only cloud models, Hermes Cloud or paid add-on tools cost money.

Takeaways

  • Most of Hermes Desktop works fine on its defaults. Three pages decide whether a local setup works: Model, Providers and Safety.
  • Local Models and ollama ps tell you whether your model really fits on your GPU.
  • Next up: Hermes sends me a daily report on Telegram using scheduled jobs. Subscribe on YouTube so you don’t miss it.

Sources

  • Hermes Agent: Desktop user guide
  • Hermes Agent: Local Ollama setup
  • Ollama FAQ (ollama ps)
  • Ollama context length

item.title: Hermes Agent Telegram Setup in 4 Steps: Control Your Local AI From Your Phone
item.description:
I sent a Telegram message from my phone, and my own PC answered. The reply came from a free AI model running locally in Ollama, with no API key and no subscription. In this post, we connect Hermes Agent to Telegram on Windows in 4 steps, then try three real things from the phone.

This is Part 2. If Hermes, Ollama and Qwen are not set up yet, start with Part 1: I Built a FREE AI Agent on My Windows PC.

🎥 Watch the Video

👉 Watch on YouTube: Hermes Agent Telegram Setup

🔗 How It Works

Your phone is the remote control. All the thinking happens on your PC.

  1. You send a message to your Telegram bot.
  2. The Hermes gateway on your PC keeps checking Telegram for new messages.
  3. Hermes hands your message to the AI model running in Ollama (Qwen 3.8).
  4. The model thinks, Hermes does the work, and the reply goes back to your phone.

The default Telegram gateway uses outbound long polling, so you do not need a public IP, a domain or a VPS for this setup.

✅ Before You Start

Hermes and Ollama must already work on your PC. My setup for this video:

Item Value
GPU RTX 4070 (12 GB VRAM)
RAM 32 GB
OS Windows 11
Model qwen3.8:27b in Ollama
Context length 64000

🤖 Step 1: Create a Telegram Bot with BotFather

  1. Open Telegram and search for BotFather. Pick the official one with the blue tick.
  2. Start the chat and send /newbot.
  3. Enter a name. This is the display name, so anything works, like My Hermes Agent.
  4. Enter a username. It must be unique and must end in bot.

BotFather now gives you a token. Treat it like your bot’s password: anyone with it can control your bot. Never share it, and never show it in a screenshot or video.

🆔 Step 2: Get Your Telegram User ID

Search for userinfobot, start the chat, and it replies with a number. That number is your user ID. You need the number, not your @username.

This is the most important security setting. Hermes denies all users by default, and only replies to user IDs you allow. Even if someone finds your bot, Hermes ignores them.

⚙️ Step 3: Run Hermes Gateway Setup

Open PowerShell and run:

1

hermes gateway setup

The wizard walks you through it:

  • Select Telegram. In my version it was option 21.
  • Choose the manual path (option 2 for me) and paste the bot token from BotFather. The terminal may look blank after you paste. The token is still entered, so press Enter.
  • Paste your user ID for allowed users.

Never leave allowed users empty. That list is what keeps your PC under your control. Hermes saves these settings on your PC, so you only do this once.

🚀 Step 4: Start the Gateway and Test 

1

hermes gateway

When the gateway is up, it reports that the Telegram adapter is connected. Keep this window open: the bot only replies while the gateway is running.

Now open your bot in Telegram, press Start and say hi. The reply comes from Qwen running on your own PC.

⏳ Tip: Use /busy queue

A local model on a 12 GB GPU can take a while to reply. If you send a new message while Hermes is still working, it treats your new message as a correction to the current task. Send this once in your bot chat:

1

/busy queue

Now new messages wait their turn and run as separate tasks. /busy status shows the current mode, and /stop cancels the running task.

📱 3 Things You Can Do From Your Phone

1. Check your PC from anywhere

Check how much free space is left on my C drive, and list the five biggest folders in my Downloads.

Hermes runs the commands on your PC and sends the answer back to Telegram.

2. Send a PDF and get a summary

Attach a PDF in the chat and ask:

Give me a five point summary of this file in simple English.

The file goes to your PC, the local model reads it, and the summary comes back to your phone.

3. Send a photo and ask what’s in it

Send a photo from your phone and ask Hermes to identify what it shows. The image is processed by the model on your PC.

Hermes can also run scheduled tasks, so you can ask it to message you with a daily reminder or report.

⚖️ Honest Limits

  • Your PC must stay on. If it is off or asleep, or the gateway window is closed, the bot cannot reply.
  • Messages travel through Telegram. The AI model runs on your PC, but your chats pass through Telegram’s servers. Keep that in mind for very private files.
  • Speed depends on your GPU. On a 12 GB card the 27B model is slow. On smaller GPUs, try qwen3.5:9b or qwen3.5:4b.

🧯 Quick Fixes

Problem Fix
Bot does not reply Check the gateway window is still open and your user ID is in allowed users
Unauthorized or invalid token Copy the token again from BotFather and re-run hermes gateway setup
Replies slow or cut off Run ollama ps and check the context is still 64000
Hermes changed what it was doing You sent a message mid-task. Use /busy queue or wait for the reply
Bot stopped overnight Your PC went to sleep. Adjust Windows power settings

Takeaways

Four steps turn your PC into a private AI agent you can reach from your phone: create the bot, get your user ID, run hermes gateway setup, and start hermes gateway. The one setting you must never skip is allowed users.

What would you ask your PC from your phone? Tell me in the comments on the video. Thanks for reading, and see you in the next one.

Sources

  • Hermes messaging gateway
  • Hermes Telegram setup
  • Hermes scheduled tasks (cron)

item.title: I Built a FREE AI Agent on My Windows PC (Hermes + Ollama + Qwen 3.8)
item.description:
You can run a free AI agent on your own Windows PC with Hermes Agent, Ollama and Qwen 3.8. It needs no API key and no subscription, and your files never leave your machine. This guide walks through the full Hermes Agent setup in 5 steps, then tests it on 3 real tasks.

What you will do:

  1. Install Ollama on Windows
  2. Download Qwen 3.8
  3. Set the context length to 64K (the step most people miss)
  4. Install Hermes Desktop
  5. Connect Hermes to Ollama

🎥 Watch the Video

👉 Watch on YouTube: I Built a FREE AI Agent on My Windows PC

🧩 How Hermes, Ollama and Qwen Work Together

A local AI agent has three parts: an agent that does the work, a model that thinks, and an engine that runs the model.

Part Role What it does
Hermes Agent The worker Decides what to do and uses tools: reading files, running commands, memory, skills
Qwen 3.8 The brain The AI model that does the thinking
Ollama The engine Runs the model on your own PC

Hermes Desktop is the app window for Hermes, so you do not need the terminal for day-to-day use. Hermes is open source and built by Nous Research.

🖥️ Hardware Requirements for Qwen 3.8

Qwen 3.8 27B runs smoothly on a GPU with about 24 GB of VRAM. On less, part of the model spills into system RAM and replies slow down. The 4-bit Ollama download is about 17 GB, and Unsloth lists 17–19 GB VRAM for 4-bit quants.

  • GPU: 24 GB VRAM recommended (for example RTX 4090)
  • RAM: 32 GB minimum
  • Disk: about 20 GB free
  • OS: Windows 10 or 11

My test machine: RTX 4070 (12 GB VRAM), 32 GB RAM, 1 TB SSD, Windows 11. That is below the recommendation, so my timings show the slow end.

Which model for your GPU

Your GPU VRAM Model to pull Download size
24 GB qwen3.8:27b ~17 GB
12–16 GB qwen3.5:9b ~6.6 GB
8 GB qwen3.5:4b ~3.4 GB

Every step below stays the same; only the model name changes.

🦙 Step 1: Install Ollama on Windows

Download the Windows installer from ollama.com and run it. If Ollama is already installed, update it: Qwen 3.8 needs a recent Ollama release. Check your version in PowerShell:

1

ollama --version

🧠 Step 2: Download Qwen 3.8

Pull the model in PowerShell. It is about 17 GB, so the time depends on your internet speed.

1

ollama pull qwen3.8:27b

Why not regular Qwen 3?

Hermes needs at least 64,000 tokens of context and refuses to start below that. On Ollama, qwen3:8b, qwen3:14b and qwen3:32b are listed with a 40K context window, so Hermes rejects them. Qwen 3.8 supports 256K, so it clears the limit easily.

⚠️ Step 3: Set Ollama Context Length to 64K

This is the step that breaks Hermes for most people. Ollama sets its default context by VRAM: 4K under 24 GB, 32K from 24–48 GB, and 256K above that. Hermes needs 64K, because every turn it sends the model its tools, skills and memory. One guide puts that at around 13,000 tokens per turn before your question.

On most Indian gaming GPUs you get 4K by default. Raise it one of two ways:

  • Ollama app: Settings → Context length slider → 64k
  • Environment variable: set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH to 64000, then restart Ollama

Verify it worked. Load the model, then run:

1

ollama ps

The CONTEXT column should read around 64000, not 4096. The PROCESSOR column shows whether the model sits fully on your GPU or is split with the CPU.

New to context size? I explain it in What Is Context Size in Ollama?

🪽 Step 4: Install Hermes Desktop on Windows

Hermes Desktop installs the app and the Hermes agent together. Get it from the Hermes desktop page.

  • Windows 11: install from the Microsoft Store or the downloaded installer
  • Windows 10: use the PowerShell installer, then open the app
1

iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)

Ollama also documents a one-command route, ollama launch hermes-desktop, in its Hermes Desktop integration guide. For Windows, it calls the desktop installer the recommended path.

🔌 Step 5: Connect Hermes Agent to Ollama

When Hermes asks for a model provider, choose the custom, OpenAI-compatible endpoint option. The label can differ slightly between versions. Enter these values:

Setting Value
Base URL http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
API key leave empty
Model qwen3.8:27b
Context length 64000

Save, send a quick “hi”, and check that Hermes replies. If it cannot connect, confirm the Ollama app is running and the URL ends in /v1.

🛠️ 3 Real Things a Local AI Agent Can Do

I tested Hermes on three everyday tasks. Copy the prompts and change the paths to your own folders.

1. Find large files eating your disk space

Find the 10 largest files in C:\Users\YourName\Downloads, list them with their sizes, and tell me which ones look safe to delete. Do not delete anything.

The last line matters. An agent can run commands on your PC, so always say what it is not allowed to do.

2. Summarise a PDF privately

Read the PDF in this folder and give me a five point summary in simple English.

This is where local AI shines. Bank statements, offer letters and client documents never leave your PC.

3. Generate a README for a project

Look at the project in C:\Users\YourName\Projects\my-app. Read the files to understand what it does, then create a README.md in the same folder with: project name and description, features, tech stack, prerequisites, how to install, how to run, and folder structure. Only create README.md. Do not change or delete any other file.

This is a true multi-step agent task: Hermes reads several files, works out the project, then writes a new file.

⚖️ Local AI vs Cloud AI: Honest Verdict

On a 12 GB GPU, Qwen 3.8 works for tasks you can wait on, not quick back-and-forth chat. The 27B model does not fit fully on my RTX 4070, so part of it runs on the CPU. In an earlier test on this machine, the same model took 34 minutes to build a snake game in Claude Code.

Local (Hermes + Ollama) Cloud API
Cost Free after hardware Pay per use or subscription
Privacy Files stay on your PC Data goes to the provider
Speed Depends on your GPU Fast
Long multi-step tasks Weaker on small GPUs Stronger

With a 24 GB GPU, Qwen 3.8 is a strong pick. With less, use the smaller Qwen 3.5 models for faster replies.

🧯 Hermes Agent + Ollama: Common Errors and Fixes

Error Cause Fix
Context window below the minimum required by Hermes Ollama still on 4K, or a 40K model like qwen3:8b Redo Step 3, check ollama ps, use Qwen 3.8 or 3.5
ollama command not found PowerShell opened before install Restart PowerShell
Very slow replies Model larger than VRAM, split across CPU and GPU Check PROCESSOR in ollama ps; use a smaller model
Hermes cannot connect Ollama not running or wrong URL Start the Ollama app; URL must end in /v1
Model forgets your request Context too small, prompt truncated Set context to 64K and restart Ollama

❓ FAQ

Is Hermes Agent free?

Yes. Hermes Agent is open source from Nous Research. With a local model through Ollama, there are no API costs.

Can I run Hermes Agent on Windows?

Yes. Hermes Desktop installs natively on Windows 11 and Windows 10. The command-line route through ollama launch hermes needs WSL2 on Windows.

What is the minimum context length for Hermes Agent?

64,000 tokens. Below that, Hermes refuses to start.

Which Qwen model is best for Hermes Agent?

Qwen 3.8 27B on a 24 GB GPU. On 12–16 GB use qwen3.5:9b, and on 8 GB use qwen3.5:4b.

Does it work offline?

The model runs entirely on your PC, so your prompts and files are not sent to a cloud AI.

Takeaways

Hermes Desktop, Ollama and Qwen 3.8 give you a real AI agent on your own Windows PC for ₹0. The one setting to remember is context length: set it to 64K, or Hermes will not work.

What would you automate with a free local AI agent? Tell me in the comments on the video. Thanks for reading, and see you in the next one.

Sources

  • Ollama docs: Context length
  • Ollama docs: Hermes Desktop
  • Ollama library: qwen3
  • Unsloth: Qwen3.8
  • Capital & Compute: Best local models for Hermes Agent
  • LumaDock: Hermes Ollama context fix
